primary_delta_manual_layer.locus: Manual of the Delta, DM 12,7-9, Sebennytos section
direct_content_as_reported_in_critical_t: The Lance of the eldest Shu and the Net (ibṯ.t) of the Divine Mother are sacred objects subject to avoidance/taboo.
The immediately following passage links ritual avoidance to women avoiding sex with their husbands when Geb sexually unites with his mother.
The lance participates in the mythic complex of Geb's sexual crime and punishment.
direct_non_content: The primary quoted sentence does not state that the Lance is a phallus.
The primary quoted sentence does not state that the Net is a vagina/vulva.
The primary quoted sentence does not state that the Lance is inserted into the Net.
The primary quoted sentence does not specify a sheath, socket, enclosure, or penetration geometry.

jorgensen_interpretive_layer.proposal: If the Sebennytos sacred-object pair works analogously to the Mendes male/female ritual complex, the Lance could represent the phallus of Shu and the Net the vagina of Tefnut.
supporting_context: Shu is associated with the lance/Onuris at Sebennytos.
The net belongs to the Divine Mother, plausibly Tefnut in this context.
The pair is embedded in a sexual-violation and punishment complex.
Jørgensen discusses a possible ritually enacted hieros gamos/reunion of the sacred objects.
jorgensen_interpretive_layer.authorial_caveat: Jørgensen explicitly frames the phallus/vagina equation with conditional language ('If something similar is the case...') and calls the support indirect.

mechanical_implication.why: A physical net is an enclosing/capturing implement, but the primary text does not say that it encloses the lance or functions as a genital analogue.
mechanical_implication.comparison_to_jumilhac: pJumilhac supplies direct retention mechanics (ḥnn + mḥ + kꜣ.t + cannot withdraw); Sebennytos supplies a separate sacred male/female object pair only at interpretation level.
mechanical_implication.comparison_to_mendes: pBrooklyn Mendes directly names a metal kꜣ.t next to a phallus/Djed context; Sebennytos does not directly name genital terms for Lance/Net.

sources.use: DM 12,7-9 quotation and author's conditional Lance/Net genital interpretation
